name: Deep500
description: We introduce Deep500: the first customizable benchmarking infrastructure that enables fair comparison of the plethora of deep learning frameworks, algorithms, libraries, and techniques. The key idea behind Deep500 is its modular design, where deep learning is factorized into four distinct levels: operators, network processing, training, and distributed training. Our evaluation illustrates that Deep500 is customizable (enables combining and benchmarking different deep learning codes) and fair (uses carefully selected metrics). Moreover, Deep500 is fast (incurs negligible overheads), verifiable (offers infrastructure to analyze correctness), and reproducible. Finally, as the first distributed and reproducible benchmarking system for deep learning, Deep500 provides software infrastructure to utilize the most powerful supercomputers for extreme-scale workloads.
evaluation_method: composite_metrics (runtime, throughput, scalability, accuracy/correctness, memory/communication overhead)
general_score_metric: composite_metrics (no single primary metric; typically throughput/runtime and correctness/accuracy are reported)
reputation: Well-cited research infrastructure for fair, modular benchmarking of deep learning frameworks and distributed training; used in systems and benchmarking research though not a mainstream dataset-style benchmark.
notes: Infrastructure-focused (non-LLM). Results depend heavily on hardware, software configuration, and workload; reproducibility at large scale requires significant engineering and access to resources.
